lesson.title: Uno, Dos, Tres: A Counting Song with Fingers
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Sol brought a brand-new song today — a counting song! Hold up your hands, because we're going to count with our fingers all the way to five.

Let's start slow. Hold up one finger and say [[uno]] — that means 'one'! Hold up a second finger and say [[dos]] — 'two'! Hold up a third finger and say [[tres]] — 'three'! Echo Sol slowly: uno... dos... tres...
Now let's go faster! Hold up a fourth finger and say [[cuatro]] — 'four'! Hold up your whole hand — all five fingers! — and say [[cinco]] — 'five'! Sing it fast now: ¡Uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco!
You counted all the way to cinco with your fingers — uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco! Tomorrow, get your hands ready to clap along with Sol.

objectives: Count aloud from uno to cinco (one to five) while raising a finger for each number
Echo the counting song at both a slow and a fast tempo
materialsNeeded: Sol the puppet (or stuffed animal/toy from weeks 1-2)
Just your two hands — no other materials needed
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Gather with Sol and hold up both hands, palms facing your child.
2. Slowly raise one finger at a time, saying uno, dos, tres together with your child, pausing after each number for the echo.
3. Raise a fourth and fifth finger, saying cuatro and cinco, until your whole hand is up.
4. Sing the counting song fast now, all five fingers going up quickly: '¡Uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco!'
5. Repeat the slow-then-fast pattern 2-3 more times, letting your child lead the fingers themselves.
6. Close by asking: 'Can you count to five with me one more time, just with your fingers?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: stop at tres (three) for the first few rounds and add cuatro/cinco once uno-dos-tres feels automatic
Ready for more: after counting up, try counting back down from cinco to uno, lowering one finger at a time
This is a listening-and-singing activity — your child never needs to see these numbers written down to learn them
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken counting-and-finger activity — success looks like your child raising fingers and attempting uno through cinco out loud, not a written right/wrong answer.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Opens week 3's ACTFL Interpretive Listening target (WA-WL-2015.1.2) — recognizing spoken numbers 1-5 — by pairing each number word with a concrete finger count, giving the child a physical anchor for a word they're only hearing, exactly the oral/aural-first approach this K-2 band calls for.
